# Champions of the Future

Champions of the Future (COTF) is an international kart racing competition organized by the RGMMC Group and sanctioned by FIA Karting (CIK-FIA). Founded in 2020, COTF is one of 11 competitions on the international kart racing calendar in CIK-FIA classes . The series has become a prominent platform for young racing talent, with several past winners progressing to careers in single-seat racing .

## History and Organization

Champions of the Future was launched in 2020 by promoter RGMMC as a new international kart racing series . The competition was designed to provide a high-quality racing platform for young drivers and teams, with the goal of identifying and developing future motorsport champions . From its inception, COTF positioned itself as a feeder series for FIA Karting events, with its calendar closely aligned with major international karting championships .

The RGMMC Group, under the leadership of President James Geidel, has established COTF as one of the premier junior karting competitions globally . The organization's approach emphasizes competitive racing combined with comprehensive support for young drivers, including live streaming of events and professional race management .

## Competition Format

### Euro Series Structure

The Champions of the Future Euro Series follows a structured format with five rounds held at premier karting circuits across Europe . The 2026 season will visit La Conca (Italy), Valencia (Spain), Mülsen (Germany), Kristianstad (Sweden), and Sarno (Italy) . The series traditionally runs from April to September, with each event featuring both OK and OK-Junior categories .

The competition format includes timed qualifying sessions, heat races, super heats, and a final race. Points are awarded based on finishing positions, with the driver accumulating the most points over the season crowned as the series champion . The 2023 season saw 170 drivers compete in OK-Junior and 142 in OK, demonstrating the series' international appeal .

### Classes and Categories

Champions of the Future primarily features two main categories:

* **OK Class**: For drivers aged 15 and above, using 125cc direct injection engines

* **OK-Junior Class**: For drivers aged 12-15, using 125cc direct injection engines with restricted performance 

The technical regulations for both classes align with FIA Karting standards, ensuring fair competition and safety . Tires are supplied by Maxxis, which became a partner of the series in 2024 .

## Notable Achievements and Winners

### Series Champions

The Champions of the Future series has produced several notable champions who have gone on to achieve success in higher levels of motorsport .

**OK-Junior Champions:**

* 2023: Lewis Wherrell (Great Britain)

* 2024: James Anagnostiadis (Great Britain)

**OK Champions:**

* 2023: Alex Powell (Jamaica)

* 2024: James Anagnostiadis (Great Britain)

### Driver Development Success

Several past COTF competitors have progressed to Formula 1 development programs:

* James Anagnostiadis, the 2024 double champion, was signed to the Mercedes Driver Development Programme shortly after his victory

* Sara Matsui earned a place in the Williams Racing Driver Academy

* Fionn McLaughlin was recruited by Red Bull Racing

These achievements underscore COTF's effectiveness as a talent identification and development platform .

### Record-Breaking Performances

The 2024 season saw several notable performances, including Dries Van Langendonck, the 2023 world champion in his category, who started from pole position and took six wins in seven heats at one event . The series has also hosted races at historic circuits such as Val d'Argenton in France, which has previously hosted battles between Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg, as well as Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc .

## Champions of the Future Academy Program

### Program Overview

The Champions of the Future Academy Program (COTFA) is a global initiative launched to increase female participation and inclusion in national and international karting competitions by breaking down financial and technical barriers to entry . The program was developed in partnership with F1 Academy and represents a significant expansion of RGMMC's karting portfolio .

The Academy Program operates on an "Arrive and Drive" concept, where all participants use standardized equipment provided by the series . This approach ensures that drivers compete on equal terms, with talent rather than equipment quality determining results.

### Structure and Categories

The Academy Program features three age-based categories :

* **Minis (8-11 years)**: Using Parolin chassis powered by TM engines

* **Juniors (11-14 years)**: Using Kart Republic chassis powered by IAME engines

* **Seniors (14-17 years)**: Using Kart Republic chassis powered by IAME engines

The 2025 international series comprised six double-header race weekends, with events held in Portugal, Spain, Italy, Slovakia, and the United Arab Emirates . The program includes cost control measures such as limited entry fees and a chassis and engine lottery system .

### 2025 Season Results

The 2025 Academy Program season concluded with championships awarded to :

* Markas Silkunas (Lithuania) in OK-N Senior

* Conor Clancy (United Arab Emirates) in OK-N Junior

* Niccolo Perico (Italy) in Mini 60

* Wynn Godschalk (United States) in Mini U10

A notable achievement was Angelina Simons Torres from Spain becoming the second female driver to win in the OK-N Junior category in 2025, following Ella Hakkinen's victory in 2024 .

### Expansion Plans

The Academy Program is expanding globally :

* **United Kingdom Launch**: A British series will begin in 2026, organized over four rounds from March to August

* **Asia Expansion**: A special event will be held at the Coloane circuit in Macau from January 16-18, 2026

* **Middle East Series**: A regional series in the United Arab Emirates will run from November to February

## Impact and Recognition

Champions of the Future has established itself as a significant platform for young racing talent development. The series' alignment with the FIA Karting calendar positions it as a crucial preparation event for world championship races . The live streaming of events, including on-board cameras and professional broadcasting, has enhanced the series' visibility and appeal to sponsors and spectators .

The Academy Program's focus on female participation has been particularly successful, with female drivers expected to comprise over 30% of participants in some programs . This initiative has received support from organizations like Motorsport UK, which launched its Girls Karting Academy in conjunction with the Champions of the Future Academy Program .

===============================================================

* * *

[![Image 56: A 21x15 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.kartcom.com/wp-content/themes/kartcom/assets/images/flags/GB.svg)](https://www.kartcom.com/en/news/2025/11/01/rgmmc-champions-of-the-future-2026-the-calendar-confirmed/)

[International](https://www.kartcom.com/news/category/international/)[COTF](https://www.kartcom.com/news/tag/cotf/)

Publiée le 23 octobre dernier, notre projection du calendrier 2026 de la Champions of the Future Euro Series n’était pas si hasardeuse… En effet, RGMMC vient d’officialiser les cinq rendez-vous de la saison prochaine, et nous avions vu juste.

![Image 57: Race calendar for the Champions of the Future Euro Series 2026](https://www.kartcom.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/kartcom_website_ksp_rgmmc_cotf_2026-scaled.webp)

La saison s’ouvrira bien sur le tracé de La Conca (Italie) les 3-6 avril. Le championnat poursuivra sa route à Valencia (Espagne) du 1er au 4 mai, avant de rejoindre Mülsen (Allemagne) du 5 au 8 juin. La série fera ensuite escale à Kristianstad (Suède) du 24 au 27 juillet, un rendez-vous désormais incontournable du karting nordique. Enfin, Sarno (Italie) accueillera la manche finale du 11 au 14 septembre, une première pour RGMMC sur le mythique circuit napolitain.

**Calendrier officiel Champions of the Future Euro Series 2026**

 – 4 avril – La Conca (ITA) : OK / OK-Junior

 – 2 mai – Valencia (ESP) : OK / OK-Junior

 – 6 juin – Mülsen (ALL) : OK / OK-Junior

 – 25 juillet – Kristianstad (SUE) : OK / OK-Junior

 – 12 septembre – Sarno (ITA) : OK / OK-Junior

Une nouvelle fois, la série Champions of the Future s’aligne étroitement sur le calendrier FIA Karting, confirmant son rôle de répétition générale avant les grands rendez-vous mondiaux.

 Cependant toujours aucune information sur un éventuel programme dédié aux KZ/KZ2 pour 2026.

Les bases sont posées : cinq circuits de référence, des paddocks déjà impatients, et une saison 2026 qui s’annonce fidèle à l’esprit de la série , exigeante, internationale, et terriblement compétitive.

5.title: Many positive signs for the 2024 opening of the international reference series – Champions of the future
5.content:
**112 drivers in OK-Junior and 81 in OK, making a total of 193, took part in the first of the five events of the Champions of the Future Euro Series 2024 in Valencia. With two weeks to go before the FIA European Karting Championship, which will also be held in Spain on the Lucas Guerrero circuit, the drivers and teams gathered a great deal of information in a variety of weather conditions, as rain followed sunshine on the day of the Finals. The RGMMC group introduced a number of new features that were much appreciated by the competitors. In sporting terms, the show was particularly intense over the three days. Ireland’s Fionn McLaughlin in the OK class and Dutchman Rocco Coronel in the OK-Junior class finally made the difference in this high-level event.**

**Expert organisation from RGMMC**

Drawing on its long experience as a promoter, the RGMMC group has once again introduced innovations to ensure that the Champions of the Future Euro Series continues to be an international event not to be missed. In addition to the new graphic presentation for the live TV coverage, the streaming provides important information for better coverage of the racing, which benefits from numerous replays to immediately review the most significant actions.

Race Control has been equipped with additional cameras, of which there were 40 in Valencia, giving the judges of fact the means to make the racing even fairer. In addition to the series partners already present in 2023, such as Minerva’s Virtual Academy, MOM, P1 Fuels, Sports TV, Pixelcom and Unipro, new agreements have been signed with OMP, Bell, ZN, Racing Spirit, B&B and STX Motorhomes.

The drivers were able to learn about the Maxxis tyres in the option and prime versions. The Asian tyre manufacturer had a team on hand to answer questions from drivers and teams. In both dry and wet conditions, the Maxxis tyres proved very popular.

#### OK: Fionn McLaughlin dominant in the Final

From Qualifying to the podium, a lot happened. A number of youngsters from the OK-Junior class immediately showed that they were capable of fighting for victory, including Britain’s Zac Drummond (Parolin Motorsport), who took pole position, Belgium’s Thibaut Ramaekers (VDK Racing) and Portugal’s Noah Monteiro (KR Motorsport). Drummond won four of the Qualifying Heats, but Brazilian Gabriel Gomez (CRG Racing Team) did even better with five wins out of five! Ramaekers won twice, with the other heats going to Anatoly Khavalkin (Parolin Motorsport), Lewis Wherrell (Forza Racing), Dmitry Matveev (KR Motorsport) and Monteiro.

Using rain tyres on a track that was drying out, Gomez held his own in Super Heat 1, while slicks returned for Super Heat 2, won by Ireland’s Fionn McLaughlin. But conditions changed again in the Final, with the return of relatively heavy rain. Drummond got off to the best start from the second row and led the first two laps, before his advantage was overturned by Joe Turney (KR Motorsport), who returned to the front as the competition wore on.

The battle was just beginning, with several other drivers highly competitive in these low grip conditions, including Gomez, McLaughlin, as well as Ukrainian Oleksandr Bondarev (Prema Racing) and Belgian Ean Eyckmans (Birel ART Racing). After a series of passes, McLaughlin made the difference and crossed the finish line victorious. Turney crashed out and retired shortly before the finish. A number of penalties altered the Final classification slightly. Initially in 2nd place, Gomez swapped places with Bondarev, but saved his place on the podium ahead of Khavalkin, Eyckmans and Drummond. Great Britain’s Noah Wolfe (VAR by Birel) made a superb comeback from 21st to 7th. Czech driver Jindrich Pesl (ASD Monster Factory Team) took 8th place ahead of Australian Xavier George Avramides (Tony Kart Racing Team).

#### OK-Junior: Rocco Coronel dominates in the rain

The 2023 World Champion in the category, Belgian Dries Van Langendonck (Forza Racing) started his meeting from pole position and went on to take six wins in seven heats. No fewer than 10 other drivers managed to win at least once: Austrian Niklas Schaufler (DPK Racing), Dutchman Rocco Coronel (Victory Lane), Briton Kenzo Craigie (Prema Racing), Spaniard Christian Costoya (Parolin Motorsport), Italian Filippo Sala (RFM), Germany’s Arjen Kraeling (KR Motorsport), Nikita Nikishov (VDK Racing), Great Britain’s Archie Lovatt (Forza Racing), Finland’s Sebastian Lehtimaki (Tony Kart Racing Team) and Great Britain’s Henry Domain (Energy Corse). In other words, there were plenty of podium contenders in Valencia!

The victories of Costoya on rain tyres and Schaufler on slicks in the Super Heats did not fundamentally change the starting grid for the Final. It began with an intense duel between Schaufler and Van Langendonck, while Frenchman Thomas Pradier (Victory Lane) had to retire from 6th position. Coronel was soon on the attack and after passing the Belgian for the first time, he got the better of the Austrian and went on to claim a deserved victory in these conditions. By finishing 2nd and 3rd respectively, Schaufler and Van Langendonck put in a good performance in the Championship.

In the chasing pack, positions changed frequently. Only 41st at the end of the Qualifying sessions, Dutchman Dean Hoogendoorn (AKM Motorsport) could be proud of his comeback in 4th position ahead of Craigie, one of the revelations of the event. 82nd on Friday and 31st after the heats, Briton Kit Belofsky (Fusion Motorsport) achieved the feat of moving up to 6th. While some of the favourites dropped out, such as Costoya and Italy’s Iacopo Martinese (KR Motorsport), Poland’s Borys Lyzen (Sodikart) moved up 28 places to 8th behind Nikishov. Sala and Lehtimaki completed the top 10.

Champions of the Future Academy to launch in the UK for 2026, offering further opportunities for Karting talent
===============================================================================================================

Tuesday 15 July 2025

This National Motorsport Week karting is a motorsport discipline that definitely deserves a mention! It’s pretty well-known that, barring a few exceptions, most of today’s top professional racing drivers all started their careers in karting.

2026 will see even more opportunities for aspiring drivers to get involved in karting, if they lack current access to high performance FIA karting equipment through: The 2026 Motorsport UK British Champions of the Future Academy Programme.

Launched in conjunction with RGMMC, a global promoter of karting events, the programme has had successful seasons in Europe and the Middle East.

Arriving in the UK in 2026, the programme will take place at four UK locations, with drivers able to compete in three classes; the Mini 60, Ages 8 – 12 (chassis – Parolin powered by TM), OK-N Junior, Ages 12-14 (chassis – Kart Republic powered by IAME) and OK-N Senior Ages 15 to 18 (chassis – Kart Republic powered by IAME) classes. All karts and engines are drawn by lottery.

The new series also acknowledges the growing number of drivers joining the sport from Motorsport UK’s “Arrive and Drive” Championships and forms another critical step in the Karting Pathway, which was established in 2020.

Buoyed on by the successful launch of [Motorsport UK’s Girls Karting Academy](https://www.motorsportuk.org/about-us/equality-diversity-and-inclusion/initiatives/girls-karting-academy/), it is expected that female drivers are set to make up over 30% of the Champions of the Future (COTF) programme, a foundation which will continue to be built upon next year.

James Geidel, President of the RGMMC Group, adds, “Following the success and validation of the Champions of the Future Academy Program International Series, the platform has firmly established itself as a launchpad for future stars in motorsport.

“Our very first Junior winner, James Anagnostiadis, was signed to the Mercedes Driver Development Programme, and just nine months later went on to become Vice Champion at the FIA Karting World Championship. Similarly, Sara Matsui earned a place in the Williams Racing Driver Academy, and Fionn McLaughlin was recruited by Red Bull Racing. These achievements underscore the Academy’s strength as a genuine talent identification platform.

“In addition, our close collaboration with the F1 Academy’s “Discover Your Drive” initiative will now extend into our national-level programmes.

“The United Kingdom, long regarded as one of the world’s premier environments for nurturing young racing talent, is the natural home for the launch of the Champions of the Future Academy Program National Series. This expansion marks an exciting new chapter in our mission to develop the next generation of racing talent.”

Dan Parker, Head of Karting, Motorsport UK, comments, “In the ever-evolving world of motorsport, the pursuit of more diverse racing opportunities and supporting promising talent are vital for the sport’s growth and sustainability.

“With four double-header events scheduled for the season, and three categories, there are now even more opportunities for aspiring talent to get involved and try out Karting for themselves.”

For more information and updates, visit the official website: [www.championskartingacademy.com](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.championskartingacademy.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7CCharlotte.Mackenzie%40motorsportuk.org%7Cbd243b623def4595b23e08dd3002b9bb%7C63a2da0237564d81baedec1930321ea4%7C0%7C0%7C638719510470622534%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=67nbw0JZEgL8Clcpb6FmNA7ga6YAYjvVYX52A3V9GXg%3D&reserved=0).

In the end, it was Ireland’s Fionn McLaughlin in the OK class and Belgium’s Dries Van Langendonck in the OK-Junior class who crossed the… [![Image 2: A grand debut in Slovakia and races full of twists and turns](https://www.championskarting.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/KSP_203_1303-1280x510.jpg)](https://www.championskarting.com/a-grand-debut-in-slovakia-and-races-full-of-twists-and-turns/) #### [A grand debut in Slovakia and races full of twists and turns](https://www.championskarting.com/a-grand-debut-in-slovakia-and-races-full-of-twists-and-turns/) Rising from the ashes in 2020, the Slovakia Ring provided the backdrop for Round 3 of the Champions of the Future Euro Series, which has now moved into the second half of the 2024 season. The uncertain weather conditions of the first day gave way to incessant duels and intense suspense, under the direction of… [![Image 3: Exciting discoveries and changing hierarchies](https://www.championskarting.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/KSP_275_4934-1280x510.jpg)](https://www.championskarting.com/exciting-discoveries-and-changing-hierarchies/) #### [**Exciting discoveries and changing hierarchies**](https://www.championskarting.com/exciting-discoveries-and-changing-hierarchies/) For the first time since its creation in 2020, the Champions of the Future Euro Series visited France, for the second of five events in this top-level competition. champions of the future
-----------------------

Launched in 2020 by promoter RGMMC, the Champions of the Future series has become a must for the best international drivers and teams. Some of the biggest names in the world have already won the competition, some of them now in single-seaters. In 2024, the Champions of the Future Euro Series will be held over five meetings optimally spread between March and September. Based on the FIA Karting regulations, this season promises to be rich in quality and quantity in the OK and OK-Junior categories.

tv highlights
-------------

[![Image 13: 6:10pm - Stream Starts 6:15pm - Qualifying Starts 6:30pm - Race Starts](https://i2.ytimg.com/vi/5Z5Zm80cegs/hqdefault.jpg) KartSim eSports | Zuera | 2025 Champions of the Future](https://www.championskarting.com/wp-content/plugins/feeds-for-youtube/img/lightbox-placeholder.png)

[![Image 14: KZ: Hiltbrand and Van Walstijn the heroes of the day The event got off to a perfect start for Danilo Albanese (KR Motorsport) with pole position, but the Italian then had to let other drivers take centre stage... Giuseppe Palomba (Maranello Kart), Mattéo Spirgel (CPB Sport) and Senna Van Walstijn (CPB Sport) shared the three heats, before Van Walstijn went on to win the Super Heat ahead of Pedro Hiltbrand (Birelart Racing). In the intermediate classification, Palomba took the lead before the Final, but was immediately overtaken by Hiltbrand after a few corners. A magnificent duel then began between Hiltbrand, Palomba and Van Walstijn, with David Trefilov lying in wait (Formula K SRP Factory Team). As the laps went by, Senna Van Walstijn proved to be the fastest, confirming this with the best lap of the race. He overtook Palomba and then Hiltbrand to cross the finish line 1st after 24 laps. However, he was given a five-second penalty, leaving the victory to Hiltbrand. Behind them, Trefilov collided with Palomba while trying to secure his place on the podium and was also penalised. Lorenzo Travisanutto (Parolin Motorsport), who had won his duel with Daniel Vasile (CL Racing Team) and then defended against Albanese's comeback, had the satisfaction of taking 3rd place. Jean Nomblot (CPB Sport) and Viktor Gustafsson (CRG Racing Team), who finished 6th and 7th respectively, also showed strong potential at Franciacorta. The list of retirements grew as the laps went by, including names such as Renaudin, Spirgel, Lorandi, Camplese, Pex, Ippolito and Denner. Although he did not win this Final, Van Walstijn consoled himself with the 2025 Champions of the Future Shifters title ahead of France's Jean Nomblot and Italy's Giuseppe Palomba, who saved 3rd place by a few points ahead of Spirgel and Hiltbrand. ![Image 24: The online school wants the student to Balance their karting and education](https://www.championskarting.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/MVA-X-RGMMC-WEBSITE-BANNER-UPDATED-2025-1600-x-300-px.png)

Minerva’s Virtual Academy offers bespoke education for racers aged 12 – 18. Unlike traditional schools, the Academy can be accessed anywhere in the world, at any time, and offers a world-class, flexible education fit for the 21st century. Pupils no longer have to miss school to attend training, track events, or race weekends.

The online school, which has won many awards since its launch, is run by Lawrence Tubb, a former head of department at Wycombe Abbey (one of the UK’s most prestigious private schools), and blends smart, interactive self-study (supported by the pupil’s personal mentor) with live online classes that can be managed around the athletes’ schedule. Young racers in particular are assisted by a unique mentoring programme that helps to develop them professionally as well as academically, overseeing their mental wellbeing whilst teaching soft skills such as public-speaking, self-confidence, and self-discipline.

Its pupils, who are able to choose from over 20 subjects at GCSE or A Level, are welcomed into a thriving, global community of talented pupils in sport and the arts, including Olympic hopefuls, West End performers, musicians, actors, and social media influencers, setting them up with brilliant friendships and connections for later on in life.

For the most bespoke solution (very popular in karting), private tutors from the school provide 1-2-1 teaching either in person or online, to ensure the pupil receives maximum attention and support on their path to success.
